A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BabyVLM work. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable, and renamed or relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, dataset augmentation experiments, language-bias ablations, and compositional analyses in Tables 3-8 and the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds larger-model evaluations, additional dataset controls, and data-efficiency curves.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a BabyLLaVA variant combining Llama-1.1B with ViT-L. The original GPT-2/ResNeXt-50 architecture, connector, three-stage training procedure, and GPT-4o/CLIP/Hungarian data-transfer pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use SAYCam and transferred data from CC3M, LAION, and SBU, with the same in-domain and out-of-domain tasks. The additional source-only and doubled-size conditions reuse these sources. Moving out-of-domain evaluations to the supplement does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 7 add BabyLLaVA-Llama as a capacity comparator alongside the original model, now named BabyLLaVA-GPT2. CVCL, CLIP-large, LLaVA-v1.5-7B, and its fine-tuned version remain in the corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The evaluation design expands beyond fixed-size mixtures: v2 adds transferred-only, random-only, and doubled-SAYCam controls, a larger model configuration, and 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% data-fraction experiments with identical training steps. These substantially extend controls over data quantity, composition, and capacity; existing benchmark metrics and test sets are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether increased capacity helps, whether transferred data can replace SAYCam, whether simply increasing SAYCam suffices, and how performance scales with training-data fractions. Table 4 and Figure 12 substantially strengthen investigation of the data-efficiency premise. Existing language-bias, compositional, and out-of-domain analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new tables and Figure 12 continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: All matched pre-existing table scores are retained. Substantial new results include BabyLLaVA-Llama scores in Tables 3 and 7, three dataset-control rows in Table 4, and fraction-dependent curves on three tasks in Figure 12. For example, the newly evaluated Llama variant scores 0.6029 on VTWT and 0.1477 on VQA; these are additional model results, not improvements to the original model.

T1.justification: The benchmark formulations, including positive- and negative-context Baby Winoground scores, are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain three SAYCam-derived benchmarks, child-directed synthetic augmentation, and BabyLLaVA. The abstract and conclusion retain the same data-efficiency and developmental-alignment claims. Naming SAYCam more precisely and replacing 'comprehensive' with 'diverse' do not materially redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the larger model's weak performance as suggesting overfitting and transferred-only results as showing SAYCam's importance as an anchor. Section 3.1 now explains CLIP filtering through image-text relevance rather than claiming it ensures developmental simplicity. The supplement also adds a sample-efficiency interpretation of Figure 12.

D1.justification: v2 adds limited procedural information: doubled SAYCam is obtained by relaxing filtering, and fraction experiments hold training steps constant. Existing appendix prompts, training stages, hardware/time disclosures, and project access information remain. The new filtering threshold, absolute step counts, and a dedicated larger-model training recipe are not supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion expands its model references to LLaVA-NeXT variants, Qwen, Mistral, Gemma, and SigLIP; ViT and TinyLlama support the added architecture. This broadens background coverage without changing the central positioning around infant-inspired, data-efficient learning.

P1.justification: v2 shortens and edits dataset explanations, standardizes model-condition names around 'filtered', and moves developmental-appropriateness and out-of-domain discussion into the supplement. These are localized revisions; the overall narrative and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel Figure 12, expands Tables 3, 4, and 7, relocates Table 7 to the supplement, and adjusts labels and emphasis. Existing pipeline diagrams, benchmark illustrations, prompt figures, and dataset examples are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: The new capacity and dataset controls make the evidence more informative, and Figure 12 directly examines sample efficiency beyond v1's fixed-size comparisons. However, its broad 25-50% sufficiency claim exceeds the plotted evidence: CVCL's VTWT results at those fractions remain below the full random-data baseline. Sparse new implementation details and Table 4's mistaken transferred-only caption further limit the gain. Overall, the added diagnostic evidence supports a modest improvement.
